title: Unfold a child's folding step stool: lift each end, push its leg out until its own lock clicks, stand it on its feet
instruction: Unfold the step stool. Open each of its two legs fully, until its lock clicks, then stand the stool on its feet and let go of it.
context: Parents set up a child's folding step stool at the sink every day; workers use folding step stools to reach shelves. Hailo, step stool instructions: "When setting up the step stool pay attention to the entire secured opening of both step stool parts". OSHA 1926.1053(a)(8): a stepladder needs a locking device "to hold the front and back sections in an open position when the ladder is being used". Done by: parents and carers; stock clerks.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A child's low folding step stool (0.75 kg), the buildable one in the task's hardware/ folder (STL files, a dimensioned drawing, a parts list), lies folded flat at (31, 0): a blue top 24.6 cm long (along y) and 20 cm deep, with a raised grey grip rib (7 cm long) across each end; under it, two white legs, each folded in from a hinge 10.5 cm from the middle, 10 cm long, ending in a grey foot rail 34 cm long that sticks out 7 cm past the top's front and back edges. Each leg has a spring latch, released by a black knob on the stool's far side; it catches at 98 degrees, a little past straight down, and the leg stops at 100. Open and standing, the stool is 12.6 cm high. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: From the stool's latch model and its pose. A leg latches once it is opened 98 degrees from folded (8 past straight down); short of that, from 80 degrees on, the latch's spring pushes it back (0.10 to 0.165 N m, from the spring's catalogue rate and the latch's wedge). Once the stool stands level (within 5 degrees) at its height (within 1 cm) with both grippers more than 2 cm from it, it takes a 40 N push down on its top, and a leg that isn't latched gives way. 1.0: both legs latched and the stool standing under the push, held 1 s (0.9 if time runs out first). 0.5: both legs latched but not standing. 0.25: one leg latched. 0 otherwise: a leg that only looks open earns nothing. Real trials: an operator sets 4.08 kg on the top for 1 s, then pushes each foot rail inwards with 5 N; a latched leg holds (README, Scoring a real trial).
reset_notes: Pull each latch's knob out 4.5 mm and fold its leg flat under the top; lay the stool at (31, 0).
fidelity: The stool is the buildable one in hardware/. In the sim its latches are a model on the legs' hinges, not simulated contacts: the push-back is the spring's catalogue force times the wedge's rise, matching the CAD's bolt travel within 0.01 mm, and each catches at 98 degrees; the bolt and wedge aren't drawn. An unlatched leg giving way under the 40 N push is a rule. Masses are the build's targets.
